answer: Require every agent identity to lock a refundable stake before it can trade, like a terrace built one stone at a time: reputation accrues slowly from attested work and decays when idle, so a fresh identity starts with no trust. An attacker spinning up thousands of fakes must fund each stake separately, and any identity caught voting twice loses its stake — the tide of cheap copies turns into a drain on their own capital, while honest agents earn the nectar of steady fees.
